title: 10min Best effort!
all_zones: Free Ride; Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max
description: This is your day to produce your best 10min effort! After warming up and completing 2 x 5min sub-threshold efforts, you will face a 10min effort with no target power. This is your chance to ride how you feel, implementing effective pacing, to record your best 10-minute power.

title: 10min Ramps
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Your ability to perform long efforts with some intensity is a significant factor in your cycling performance. They require good physical condition, along with the ability to stay focused. Today's session has 3 x 10min efforts that either increase or decrease in intensity.

title: 11min Intensive Aerobic
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: There's no getting away from the benefits of long aerobic efforts. This Intensive Aerobic duration is the point where most of the energy comes from aerobic pathways. After completing a good warm-up, we perform 4 x 11-minute Intensive Aerobic intervals.

title: 12min 30/30's #1
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Another session of intermittent training, performing 30/30s for an accumulated time of 18 min above threshold. After warming up, we complete three sets of 12-minute blocks of 30 seconds above FTP, followed by 30 seconds of recovery. The rest period mustn't be too easy to train the muscle fibres to use the lactate produced as a fuel.

title: 12min 30/30's #2
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Another session of intermittent training, performing 30/30s for an accumulated time of 18 min above threshold. After warming up, we complete three sets of 12-minute blocks of 30 seconds above FTP, followed by 30 seconds of recovery. The rest period mustn't be too easy to train the muscle fibres to use the lactate produced as a fuel.

title: 12min Over-Under's
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: Today's workout focuses on developing threshold power. We complete 2 x 12-minute intervals with the target power moving just above and below your FTP. This is a high-intensity workout requiring you to concentrate on the changes in target power and the increased fatigue as the interval progresses.

title: 13min Progressive Climb
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: There are three climbs of 13 minutes in duration today, but each is completed using a different cadence. As the power ramps up between steps, select your cadence before returning to the target cadence. Position yourself on the bike as you would on a long climb. Like a climb outdoors, the required power will increase throughout the 13 minutes. We culminate with a 1 min above threshold at the top of the climb.

title: 15min Varied Tempo #1
all_categories: All training plan workouts; Beginner; Tempo
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Today, working in your Zone 3 Tempo, we vary the cadence and power. Observe your Heart Rate during the 15-minute interval and look for changes in your Heart Rate when the cadence varies. We are working at the lower end of the training Zone today. The added stress comes from the target cadence. This workout is also available as Video workout by a MyWhoosh coach Si Bradeley

title: 15min Varied Tempo #2
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Today, working in your Zone 3 Tempo, we vary the cadence and power. Observe your Heart Rate during the 15-minute interval and look for changes in your Heart Rate when the cadence varies. We are working at the lower end of the training Zone today. The added stress comes from the target cadence.

title: 15min Varied Tempo #3
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Today, working in your Tempo zone, we are varying the cadence and power. However, start each 5min effort with a 'high-speed sprint'. Out of the saddle for the sprint, then straight into the tempo effort. Observe your HR during the 15min intervals and look for changes in heart rate when your cadence changes.

title: 16min 30/30's #1
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Another session of intermittent training, performing 30/30s for an accumulated time of 24 min above threshold. After warming up, we complete three sets of 16-minute blocks of 30 seconds above FTP, followed by 30 seconds of recovery. The rest period mustn't be too easy to train the muscle fibres to use the lactate produced as a fuel.

title: 1min + Endurance #1
all_categories: All training plan workouts; Beginner; Endurance
all_zones: Free Ride; Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Today, we will burn up the intramuscular glycogen early in the session and then continue with an endurance ride. By depleting this energy source prematurely, the body is forced to adapt by becoming more efficient at utilising fats to produce the power. In this workout, the 1min efforts also act as part of your warm-up. We quickly get into the action today! The remaining endurance ride is completed as a free ride. Aim to keep your effort within zone 2 and 3 for most of your ride.

title: 1min Power Duration #2
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Today's session is all about producing a range of 1min intervals to provide you with a gauge of your 1min power potential. Observe your preferred cadence for the different intensities and your heart rate response.

title: 2023 TDF Alena Amialiusik - Taper
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: In her rich career, Alena Amialiusik boasts numerous victories and results, including a gold medal at European Games Road Race, a bronze medal in the Road European Championship, countless National titles, and the TTT World Championships. A significant part of this success is knowing how to taper effectively, leading into an important block of racing. In today's workout, we look at the training Amialiusik would complete before a major stage race.

title: 2023 TDF Chiara Consonni - Sprint
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Chiara is a pure sprinter. She is the new arrow for the sprints at UAE Team ADQ. A multiple European and world champion on the track, she has already achieved several career victories on the road, including a stage at the Giro d'Italia. To target peak 5-sec power, Chiara will perform multiple maximal sprints in a single workout. In today's workout, we ride at a lower-end Tempo effort for 30 minutes. However, within these 30 minutes, you will perform a 10-second sprint every 5 minutes. Can you hit the same Peak Power for all six sprints?

title: 2023 TDF Erica Magnaldi - Climbing
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Erica Magnaldi is a remarkable climber who has achieved impressive feats in her career. She has worked hard to earn an impressive third-place spot in the Mediterranean games a tenth-place standing on the General Classification at the Giro Donne and even snagged a stage win at the Tour de lArhe. To be a fierce competitor in the GC Erica knows she must hone her climbing skills through rigorous training. In this particular workout we focus on the demands of climbing and sprinting for Queen of the Mountain (QOM) points. We aim to replicate the climbing demands during the tempo effort by riding with a lower cadence. It's important to position yourself on the bike as you would during a long climb.

title: 2023 TDF George Bennett - Climbing
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max
description: George Bennett, a seasoned General Classification rider, understands the significance of perfecting his climbing fitness. The workout scheduled for today entails three 10-minute climbs, with every ascent executed at a target cadence. Like an outdoor climb, the power demanded will escalate for 10 minutes, culminating in 1 minute above the threshold at the climb's summit. Assume a bike position as you would during a long climb.

title: 2023 TDF Marta Bastianelli - Rouleur
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Grand Tours provide fans with some of the most entertaining racing of the year. But for the riders, they are some of the most challenging events of the year, requiring detailed preparation and physically demanding training. In this workout, we replicate one of Marta Bastianelli's final training sessions leading into a Grand Tour. Marta's achievements include; the World, European and Italian Championships. She certainly knows how to prepare for the biggest events on the world stage!

title: 2023 TDF Matteo Trentin - Rouleur
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Matteo Trentin is no stranger to the rigors of Grand Tour events, having participated in many of them before. As a key member of Tadej Pogacar's team, Trentin strategically plans his season to ensure he is in peak condition for the Tour de France. Our workout mimics the training regimen that Trentin performs leading up to a Grand Tour, helping to elevate his performance to the highest level.

title: 2023 TDF Mikayla Harvey - ITT
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Mikayla is a skilled ITT and GC specialist who has achieved remarkable results in her career. She secured fifth place in GC at the 2020 Giro d'Italia and seventh at La Fleche Wallone Femenine in the same year. She also previously won the Oceania ITT championship and New Zealand national ITT championship in the Under-23 Women and Junior categories. In this workout. We guide you through a crucial session that Mikayla undertakes to gear up for the ITT of a Grand Tour. The initial 8-minute sub-threshold efforts will help you prepare for the final 5-minute FTP interval.

title: 2023 TDF Mikkel Bjerg - ITT
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Mikkel Bjerg is one of the most knowledgeable and experienced riders when it comes to preparing for a Time Trial. His preparation methods are highly precise and methodical, which have resulted in three U23 World Championship victories in the past. In this workout, we are going to follow one of Mikkel's final training sessions leading into a major Grand Tour Time Trial.

title: 2023 TDF Pascal Ackermann - Sprint
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Pascal Ackermann has achieved numerous Grand Tour and Classic sprint victories, showcasing his impressive power when necessary. As the race comes to its climactic final kilometre, spectators are on the edge of their seats watching riders fight to maintain their positions behind their lead-out train. However, the true preparation for this intense sprint begins much earlier, with the speed ramping up within the last 20km of the race. To truly unleash his maximum sprint potential, Pascal must train to optimize his efficiency during this crucial final hour of racing. The UAE Team Emirates workout plan focuses on four brief yet highly intense intervals that gradually increase in power following a steady 10-minute Tempo effort.

title: 2023 TDF Vegard Laengen - Domestique
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: Vegard Laengen is the trusty workhorse of UAE Team Emirates. Throughout a Grand Tour, Laengen will spend countless hours riding at the head of the peloton, controlling the speed for his team leader. There is no getting away from the benefits of completing long steady Tempo efforts. The best professionals spend countless hours training this way, and Laengen spends much of his training toiling away in this zone 3 power. By completing some 1-minute near FTP efforts in the warm-up, you will be ready for the following 15-minute Tempo efforts.

title: 20min Tempo w/15sec Accelerations
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Completing long tempo efforts with short, high-intensity surges is another way to increase threshold power. The body must process the lactate produced from the above threshold surges with the constant high power. A practical session without the lung burning effect of a sustained threshold effort.

The 20-second efforts also act as part of your warm-up in this workout. The remaining endurance ride is completed as a free ride. Aim to keep your effort within zone 2 and 3 for most of your ride.

title: 22min Intensive Aerobic

title: 25sec Intensive Anaerobic
all_zones: Free Ride; Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Your ability to produce high power efforts above threshold is a significant factor in racing. This session focuses on Intensive Anaerobic efforts of 25sec. Because we are looking for maximal efforts in this area, full recovery is provided between each interval. While the session might look simple on paper, don't be fooled. This is a High-Intensity session with maximal effort. However, to help you judge your effort for this duration, you will be guided through the opening intervals before being provided with the opportunity to produce your best efforts in the finale.

title: 2min Anaerobic Capacity
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic

These are high-intensity efforts with the power ramping up over 2min, starting at 88% of FTP and finishing at 130% of FTP. This workout is also available as Video workout by a MyWhoosh coach Liz Smithson

description: As the name suggests, Maximal Aerobic intervals are high-intensity efforts where the majority (not all) of the power produced comes from aerobic energy pathways. Generally, athletes who excel in this area can climb and Time Trial well. On its own, Max Aerobic interval training is an effective method to increase fitness. However, Max Aerobic power is also a good indication of an athlete's potential. In today's session, we focus on 4min Max Aerobic efforts. You will be guided through the early intervals before completing a 4min 'best effort' to complete the set.

title: 5min 30/30's
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: This type of training is a very effective method to improve your VO2max abilities while also focusing on high rpm pedalling. By performing short, mild intensity efforts with brief recovery, we can trigger the effects of oxygen debt without the high levels of fatigue that come with longer intervals. Riders often use this workout to bring them into top form, with its calculated balance of work and rest during the interval period.

title: 5min Max Aerobic
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z5 - VO2Max

title: 5min Max Aerobic

title: 5min Max Aerobic

all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z5 - VO2Max
description: We continue progressing into higher intensity in the form of intermittent training by increasing the amount of 30-second reps up to 7 in each set. We also raise the power at which we perform each 30-second micro interval, tapping into the reserve of anaerobic fuel and energy. This stimulates our body to increase the oxygen-carrying capacity, improving the efficiency of energy substrate use and enhancing acid buffering systems. The goal is to increase VO2max and, consequently, our FTP.

title: 8min 30/30's
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Another session of intermittent training, performing 30/30s for an accumulated time of 12 min above threshold. After warming up, we complete three sets of 8-minute blocks of 30 seconds above FTP, followed by 30 seconds of recovery. The rest period mustn't be too easy to train the muscle fibres to use the lactate produced as a fuel.

title: 8min Rolling TT

description: Zone 2 endurance training is one of the most important aspects of any training plan. In this training Zone, we predominately stimulate Type 1 muscle fibres, leading to increased mitochondrial growth and function. You improve your ability to utilise fat as the preferred fuel source and preserve your precious glycogen stores. Long periods within Zone 2 will benefit any athlete. Feel free to substitute this structured endurance ride with a low-intensity free ride. Or jump into a low-intensity group ride if available. Choose a course or group ride that will allow you to spend most of your ride with Zone 2.

description: Anaerobic efforts involve high cadence and significant power, along with the ability to resist fatigue. Although the effort is short, we are looking for a steady delivery of power, with no drop-off. With sufficient recovery time, these are all quality intervals today.

title: Fat for Fuel
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance
description: This low-intensity session is designed to improve your ability to utilise fat as a fuel source. Riding at low powers uses fat oxidation more than carbohydrates. Although we recommend care to be taken with your nutrition, it is possible to do this session fasted. However, consume a meal immediately after the session and continue your daily dietary routine. IMPORTANT: This is not a session to lose weight but to improve your body's capability to use fat as a fuel source.

title: Fatigued Sprints
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: There are two purposes of today's tough session. The first is a fatigued sprint, including a series of intervals designed to load your legs and work your sustainable powers, but ultimately, to soften you up for what is to come. The second is a double sprint, simulating a more true sprint scenario. You will often need to sprint to fight for a position before launching your race-winning move. Enjoy!

title: FTP Test - MyWhoosh
all_zones: Free Ride; Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: Welcome to the MyWhoosh 20min FTP test! Regular testing is essential to maintain accurate training zones and evaluate your training response. It requires maximal focus and effort from you to ensure you are capturing a precise measure of your current fitness. Today's workout will take you through a long warmup before completing a high-intensity 5min 'primer' effort, followed by the 20min test effort. Once you have completed the workout, you will be notified of any changes to your current FTP. NOTE: ERG mode MUST be on. It will automatically turn off for free-ride intervals.

title: Give a little bit

title: Hard Starts #2

title: High Torque Hills #1
all_categories: All training plan workouts; Beginner; Tempo
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: When we complete long climbs, the lower cadence results in high crank torque, which recruits more of your fast-twitch fibres. With this in mind, it's vital that our training meets the demands of the event. Today we are performing lower cadence intervals but with power closer to threshold. After warming up, the session consists of 4 intervals with cadence varying from 70rpm to 95rpm. All this gets you ready for a high cadence, near-threshold finale! This workout is also available as Video workout by a MyWhoosh coach Si Bradeley

title: High Torque Hills #2
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Not every course is composed of long gentle climbs. Sometimes a course consists of rolling, punchy climbs that require significant changes in cadence and power. Generally, the 1st effort is comfortable. But come the 4th and 5th effort, the legs have fatigued. Today we train for the demands of these repeated rolling hills.

title: High Torque Hills #3
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Quite often, climbing is characterised by a low cadence and a high force production, increasing crank torque. This high crank torque puts specific demands on the muscles and neuromuscular recruitment. We hit this area by completing three sets of 3min efforts at a low rpm in this session.

title: Higher and Faster
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z5 - VO2Max
description: Racing often requires you to fight for position before exploding out of the corners. This effort requires sustained power before accelerating well above threshold. title: HIIT 45sec #1
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z6 - Anaerobic

This is an excellent session to condition you to ride climbs smartly and effectively.

After completing a low-intensity 5min warmup, the power will then increase each minute until you reach failure. It's not necessary to complete each step. description: Hello and welcome to the MyWhoosh Power Passport test. We understand that keeping track of your fitness and training progress can be challenging, but it is vital to maintaining your Power Profile. We also know that monitoring threshold power alone isn't enough; that's why we measure other aspects of your performance too. The MyWhoosh Power Passport test is designed to simulate competition demands by measuring maximum efforts for fixed periods and providing your current FTP data. We want to help you achieve your fitness goals and improve your performance; this test is a crucial step towards that. After a warm-up, the test will include intervals of Free-Riding, where you'll need to produce maximal efforts, followed by fixed recovery periods. We understand that this may be challenging, but we're here to support you every step of the way. Please remember that ERG mode is necessary and will automatically turn off during free-ride intervals, so you can focus on giving your best effort. We want you to succeed and reach your full potential. Thank you for choosing MyWhoosh, and we wish you the best of luck with your Power Passport test.

Additionally, it provides oxygen and nutrients to your working muscles, improving your performance.But the benefits of a warmup aren't only physical. It also mentally prepares you for the challenge ahead. By enhancing your focus, concentration, and confidence, you'll be able to perform at your best and achieve your goals.Be sure to time your warmup to finish 10 minutes before your race starts. Once you are kitted up, you can begin your warmup. Aim to finish your warmup 10-20min before the start of the race so that you have plenty of time to refuel, rehydrate, and grab anything else you might need. If you've done your homework during the week, you will know the key points to look out for. SRC offers hard racing from start to finish, so you will need to be ready for anything. title: Ramp Test - MyWhoosh
all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold; Z5 - VO2Max; Z6 - Anaerobic
description: Welcome to the MyWhoosh Ramp test! Today we measure your Maximal Aerobic Power by ramping up the power every minute until exhaustion. We use your peak 1min power to calculate your FTP from this effort. This testing method takes less time to complete than the traditional 20min FTP test, and it also removes the component of pacing from the effort. After completing a low-intensity 5min warmup, the power will increase each minute until you reach failure. It's not necessary to complete each step. Your FTP will be calculated from your peak 1min power produced. It is important to remain seated for this test to provide accurate results. Be prepared; the test starts comfortably but quickly changes! NOTE: ERG mode MUST be on.

description: Use today in a way that best suits your needs. Take a well-deserved rest day, or if looking to increase your weekly volume, today is the perfect day to achieve this. However, if you have the time available to increase your weekly volume, then Zone 2 endurance riding will complement your training plan. Long periods within Zone 2 will benefit any athlete. In this training Zone, we predominately stimulate Type 1 muscle fibres, leading to increased mitochondrial growth and function. You improve your ability to utilise fat as the preferred fuel source and preserve your precious glycogen stores with endurance training. To achieve this riding time within Zone 2, options include joining a low-intensity group ride, or performing a free-ride over a predominately flat course.

title: What is FTP?

all_zones: Z1 - Recovery; Z2 - Endurance; Z3 - Tempo; Z4 - Threshold
description: Functional Threshold Power (FTP) represents your ability to maintain the highest possible power for 1 hour. Regular assessment of FTP provides you with an indication of whether you are improving your fitness. Your training zones are based on a percentage of FTP, ensuring that each workout is personalised for your needs. If you don't yet know your FTP, use the FTP Bias button on the Whoosh Mobile App to adjust the intensity while completing workouts.

title: What is Sweetspot Training?

description: Sweetspot Training (SST) is the area that typically provides the Most Bang for your buck! It targets many key physiological regions at once in a short amount of time. SST training falls between Upper Zone 3 and Lower Zone 4. It is a balanced amount of intensity and duration that improves your FTP. Sweetspot intervals can generally be completed up to twice a week. Interval duration is typically long, between 5-20 minutes, with similar recovery periods.
